es: Reconocer cuándo una respuesta amable en inglés equivale a un rechazo o a un desacuerdo y entender su significado real.

teaching.en: An indirect refusal such as “I am afraid that might be difficult” spares the listener's feelings, but it rarely opens a negotiation.
teaching.es: Un rechazo indirecto como «Me temo que eso podría ser difícil» ahorra disgustos al oyente, pero rara vez abre una negociación.
teaching.explanationEs: Suavizador + vaguedad sin alternativa suele significar «no».
segments: An indirect refusal such as “I am afraid that might be
difficult” spares the listener's feelings, but it rarely opens a negotiation.
teaching.audioText: An indirect refusal such as “I am afraid that might be difficult” spares the listener's feelings, but it rarely opens a negotiation.

teaching.en: “We must have lunch sometime” is a polite brush-off, not an invitation, unless a day and a place follow.
teaching.es: «Tenemos que comer juntos algún día» es un rechazo cortés y vago, no una invitación, a menos que sigan un día y un lugar.
teaching.explanationEs: Sin día ni hora no hay plan real.
segments: “We must have lunch sometime” is a polite brush-off, not
an invitation, unless a day and a place follow.
teaching.audioText: “We must have lunch sometime” is a polite brush-off, not an invitation, unless a day and a place follow.

teaching.en: A tactful manager who says “I will think about it” without a date may simply turn down your idea.
teaching.es: Un jefe con tacto que dice «Lo pensaré» sin dar fecha puede estar rechazando simplemente tu idea.
teaching.explanationEs: «I will think about it» sin plazo suele ser un no cortés.
segments: A tactful manager who says “I will think about it”
without a date may simply turn down your idea.
teaching.audioText: A tactful manager who says “I will think about it” without a date may simply turn down your idea.

teaching.en: To be honest, “with respect” rarely introduces praise; it usually warns you that a disagreement is coming.
teaching.es: Siendo sincero, «con todo respeto» rara vez introduce un elogio; suele avisar de que llega un desacuerdo.
teaching.explanationEs: With respect anuncia un desacuerdo, no admiración.
segments: To be honest, “with respect” rarely introduces praise; it
usually warns you that a disagreement is coming.
teaching.audioText: To be honest, “with respect” rarely introduces praise; it usually warns you that a disagreement is coming.

teaching.en: Learners who take the hint hear the doubt behind a polite refusal and stop asking instead of waiting for a clearer answer.
teaching.es: Quienes captan la indirecta oyen la duda tras un rechazo cortés y dejan de insistir en vez de esperar una respuesta más clara.
teaching.explanationEs: Take the hint: entender lo que se insinúa sin que se diga.
segments: Learners who take the hint hear the doubt behind a polite
refusal and stop asking instead of waiting for a clearer answer.
teaching.audioText: Learners who take the hint hear the doubt behind a polite refusal and stop asking instead of waiting for a clearer answer.

teaching.en: A tactful person who wants to leave the door open will always add an alternative, such as “perhaps next month”.
teaching.es: Una persona con tacto que quiere dejar la puerta abierta siempre añade una alternativa, como «quizá el mes que viene».
teaching.explanationEs: La alternativa concreta es lo que distingue un «quizá» real de un «no» amable.

prompt.es: Lee la escena: ¿qué suele significar la respuesta de la vecina?

choices.text: She will certainly bring the ladder on Saturday morning, before lunch.
It is probably a polite no, since she offers no other day.
She will lend it if Leo asks again on Sunday.

feedback.es: Un «I am afraid» con un obstáculo vago y sin día alternativo es la estructura típica de un rechazo cortés.

hint.es: Fíjate en que no propone ninguna alternativa concreta.

origin.text: Leo asked his neighbour to lend him a ladder on Saturday. She smiled and said, “I am afraid it is a little awkward this weekend, but I will see what I can do.” She did not mention another day.

prompt.es: Completa: «No quería rechazar la oferta con brusquedad.»

feedback.es: Turn down es el verbo frasal habitual para rechazar una oferta o una invitación.

origin.text: The company could not afford the project, but it did not want to ___ the offer rudely, so the director wrote a warm and rather vague reply.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase indirecta con lo que suele significar.

pairs: I am afraid that might be difficult
With respect, I see it differently

feedback.es: Las tres primeras se leen como rechazos o desacuerdos; la última deja abierta una posibilidad real.

hint.es: Busca en cada frase si hay una fecha o una alternativa.

pairs: I am afraid that might be difficult
With respect, I see it differently

prompt.es: Escucha la anécdota: ¿qué hace que su respuesta equivalga a un rechazo?

choices.text: He said that another appointment made the weekend impossible.
He praised the plan but offered no other date.
He accepted and then cancelled on the same morning.
He asked the writer to send the invitation again in writing.

feedback.es: Elogia el plan, pero no propone otra fecha ni se compromete: esa ausencia de alternativa es la pista de un rechazo cortés.

origin.audio: When I invited my colleague to the company picnic, he said that it sounded lovely and that he would like to come in principle, but that the weekend was a little difficult for him. I waited for him to suggest another date, but he only smiled and asked about the weather. Later I realised that he had turned me down, as politely as possible.

prompt.es: Lee el correo: ¿qué hace realmente quien escribe con su mensaje?

choices.text: The writer accepts the proposal with some doubts.
The writer asks the client for a new deadline.
The writer disagrees politely with the proposal.
The writer changes her mind because of the client's pressure.

feedback.es: «With respect» anuncia el desacuerdo y «I wonder whether» lo suaviza; proponer hablar el lunes es cortesía, no aceptación.

origin.text: With respect, I am not sure that moving the deadline is the best option. I appreciate the client's pressure, but I wonder whether the team has enough time to do the work well. Perhaps we could discuss it on Monday.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Un rechazo con tacto deja la puerta abierta a otro día.»

answer.text: A tactful refusal leaves the door open for another day

feedback.es: El sujeto es a tactful refusal; leaves the door open expresa que se ofrece una alternativa.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato: ¿qué aprende quien narra sobre los elogios en inglés?

choices.text: That managers in London reject ideas without ever saying why.
That people in London rarely mean what they say to strangers.
That a neighbour's vague invitation is best taken at face value.
That polite praise can hide doubt, so tone and context matter.

feedback.es: «Brave» sonaba a elogio, pero en ese tono significaba «probablemente un error»: aprendió a escuchar lo que no se dice, sin concluir que nadie habla en serio.

origin.audio: When I first moved to London, I kept a list of phrases that confused me. My manager's “I will think about it” meant no. A neighbour's “we must have a drink sometime” was just goodbye. The worst was a colleague who called mine a very “brave” idea. I thanked him warmly, went home happy and spent the weekend developing it. On Monday my manager quietly removed it from the agenda. Only then did a friend explain that brave, in that tone, means “probably a mistake”. Since then I listen to what people do not say as carefully as to what they do.

prompt.es: ¿Qué quiere decir en realidad quien escribe este correo?

choices.text: The proposal is rejected, and the writer hopes to end the matter kindly.
The proposal may be accepted when the company's priorities change.
The writer wants Jordan to rewrite it for another department next year.
The writer is asking him to wait a few more weeks.

feedback.es: «Somewhere» y «elsewhere» lo sitúan fuera de su empresa, y pedirle que no invierta más tiempo es el rechazo definitivo con cortesía.

origin.text: Dear Jordan, thank you for the proposal. I can see that a great deal of work went into it, and I am sure it will find a good home somewhere. At the moment, however, our priorities lie elsewhere, and I would not want you to spend more time on it on our account. I hope that we can keep in touch.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si no te dan fecha, capta la indirecta y busca otra salida.»

feedback.es: Take the hint es la expresión fija para captar lo que se insinúa sin que se diga.

origin.text: If you have asked twice and still have no date, it is time to take the ___ and find another way forward.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su significado real según la situación.

pairs: “That is an interesting idea,” said after a two-minute pitch
“I will think about it and call you on Thursday,” said while writing in a diary

pairs.es: es una respuesta provisional con plazo real

pairs: “With respect…” at the start of a reply
“I cannot on Friday; could we try Monday?”

feedback.es: La misma fórmula cambia según el contexto: una fecha o una alternativa concreta convierte el rechazo en una posibilidad real.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la postura de quien escribe ante la indirección en inglés?

choices.text: The writer finds the soft style dishonest and avoids English speakers whenever possible.
The writer now reads the soft style as courtesy, though clarity is still preferred.
The writer has copied the indirect style and dislikes clear answers.
The writer thinks that every soft answer hides a secret refusal.

feedback.es: Ya no cree que una respuesta suave sea una mentira, pero sigue prefiriendo la claridad: comprensión sin adoptar el estilo.

origin.text: In my country, a direct “no” is a sign of honesty. In England I learnt to hear something else in “perhaps”. It took me a year to see that nobody was being dishonest; they were protecting the relationship, not hiding the truth. I still prefer a clear answer, but I no longer think that a soft one is a lie.

answer.text: They were not lying; they were being tactful

feedback.es: Were being + adjetivo describe una actitud del momento: tactful explica por qué la respuesta era suave.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje: ¿es probable que la hablante asista a la fiesta?

choices.text: Yes: she will arrive late, but she will certainly come.
Yes: she only needs Sara to send the invitation again.
Probably not: she promises nothing and suggests no alternative.
Probably: she will confirm as soon as she finishes work.

feedback.es: Elogia el plan pero no se compromete, no da fecha y no propone otra ocasión: es un rechazo cortés, no un sí aplazado.

origin.audio: Hi Sara, thanks for the invitation to your party. It sounds wonderful, and I would love to be there if I can. The week is a bit crowded at the moment, so I cannot promise anything. I will let you know if things change.
